blocks.text: Dear Mary,

Following up on Julie's note from Monday: the briefing deck is done. It covers the material we have reviewed, what came out of the first round of leadership interviews, and the directions we see for the {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} positioning statement.
The directions need some explanation, so I would like to walk you through the deck on a call before it goes any further. To set that up, I need three things from you:

1. A time for a one-hour call, either tomorrow afternoon or Monday morning.
2. The names of anyone else who should join. If someone will sign off on the final language, it is worth having them on this call.
3. Your preference on whether the deck goes to the wider leadership team after the call or waits for a revised version.
Send me a time that works and I will put the invitation out the same day.

Regards,
Daniel
Mary,

Of the two times Daniel offered, this afternoon suits us better, and I will join for the first half hour. It would help us to hear early how each direction sits with the people at {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} who will eventually have to present it.

When we go through the deck, one test is worth keeping in mind. We have weighed each option by how it holds up when an investor or a reporter asks the follow-up question, and if that has made any of them read as too cautious, we would like you to tell us.
If this afternoon works on your side, please reply to Daniel with a time and he will send the invitation.

Thanks,
JH
Dear Mary,
Thank you for the time on Friday afternoon. Confirming what we agreed on the call, so that we are all working from the same list:

1. The positioning statement will lead with the operating record, the first direction in the deck.
2. The second direction stays in reserve. We will not develop it further unless the leadership comments point back to it.
3. The combined approach, with separate wording for investors and for the press, is set aside.
4. You will collect comments on the deck from the {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} leadership team and send them to me as one set.
5. We start drafting the statement and its supporting points once those comments are in.
Quick one: is there a date by which your leadership team needs to see a draft? If so, I will plan the drafting back from it.

Regards,
Daniel
Mary,

Daniel's list matches my notes from Friday, with one qualification on the first point. Leading with the operating record does not mean dropping where the company is headed; we will keep a sentence on direction in every version, so that investors read the record as having a plan behind it.

On timing, we can work to any date your leadership team sets. Without one, we would aim to get a first draft to you by the end of next week, which leaves room for a round of comments before it is shared more widely.
Please send over the comments from the {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} leadership team when you have them, and Daniel will start the draft.

Thanks,
JH

blocks.text: The draft statement

Daniel Valenzuela took us through the first draft, which leads with the company's operating record and closes with a sentence on where the company is headed, as agreed after the briefing deck review. Mary Frank reported that the leadership team's comments were broadly supportive.

The leadership team's main reservation concerned the second supporting point, which in their view claims somewhat more than the company can document at present. We agreed that the point should be narrowed to what existing records can support, and Daniel will propose two alternative wordings for the leadership team to choose between.
Evidence behind the claims

Most of the session was given to the evidence for each claim in the draft. Mary Frank will confirm which operating figures the company is prepared to cite publicly; until she does, the draft will use descriptive language and carry no figures.

Julie Hill asked that any figure eventually used be checked against what the company has said in its most recent investor materials. A figure that differs from an earlier public statement would invite questions we would then have to answer separately, and we would prefer to settle that before the draft travels.
Media preparation

Michelle Rose presented a working media list of reporters who have covered the company or its sector, with notes on how each prefers to be approached. We agreed that no outreach will begin until the statement is final, and that the first conversations will be background briefings rather than announcements.
Mary Frank asked that her team see the list before anyone is contacted. Michelle will send it to her for review, and we will not add names to it without her agreement.
Order of audiences

We also discussed who should see the statement first. Our shared view is that the company's own staff should hear the new language before it appears in anything external, so that no one inside reads about it first in a press release.
Mary Frank will advise how internal announcements are normally handled at the company, and we will fit the rollout to that route rather than propose a new one.
Actions

rows: Propose two narrower wordings for the second supporting point
Confirm which operating figures may be cited publicly
Check the draft against current investor materials once figures are confirmed
Send the working media list to the {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} team for review
Advise on the usual route for internal announcements
Review the revised draft before it goes to the leadership team
